solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Annoyed with nation's sport

parts.note: annoyed means cross
a nation is a country; the possessive just glues the pieces to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by the national game of their country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-country running over open terrain is an athletic event, so it counts as a sport.

clue.text: Gut feeling commanding officer is over defeat mostly

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another comes before it
mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: to lick an opponent is to defeat them

explanation.surface: An officer's instinct that a defeat is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gut feeling' reads as instinct but means a literal pain in the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, literally a feeling in the gut.

clue.text: Clothes shop known to have better suiting?

parts.note: when a secret is out it is known
fitter means more suitable, better suiting

explanation.surface: A tailor's shop reputed to offer better suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' joins the pieces; 'suiting' hints at suits but means fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter sells clothing and equipment, so it is a clothes shop.

clue.text: Being on top of exceptionally good job

parts.note: super means excellent
a position is a job

explanation.surface: Being the best at an excellent job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Superposition is the placing of one thing on top of another.

clue.text: People regularly touchy about trophy

indicators.note: about puts the picked letters round the trophy word
regularly picks every other letter of the word touchy

parts.note: a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: Sensitive people repeatedly fussing over a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'touchy', and 'about' wraps them round the trophy. 'People' looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning to populate.
explanation.definitionFit: To people a place is to fill it with inhabitants, i.e. to occupy it.

clue.text: Peaceful response son earns going around

indicators.note: going around here signals the letters being moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A calm reaction when a son brings home money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges SONEARNSGOING.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-aggression pact is an agreement not to attack, a peaceful stance.

clue.text: Regret starting running up Everest

indicators.note: starting points us to the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A climber's regret about racing up Everest.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to wish it had not happened, to feel regret.

clue.text: Steal tin at church

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: Pinching a tin kept at a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch is to grab quickly, often meaning to steal.

clue.text: The French lay back for break

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

indicators.note: placed after lay, back asks for that word's synonym to be read the other way

parts.note: to lay something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A French sentence or phrase reversed to signal a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses only the synonym for 'lay'; the French article stays as it is in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing off, i.e. a break in some activity.

clue.text: Is youngster up to finding restaurant?

parts.note: to be up to doing something is to be able to, so 'can'
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: Asking whether a young person can manage to track down somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a question, 'Is youngster up to' is 'Can teen?': 'Is ... up to' together give CAN, with 'Is' riding along; 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a workplace or school dining room, a kind of simple restaurant.

clue.text: Letter from abroad from Charlie with greeting

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A letter sent from overseas by Charlie, with a friendly hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from abroad' is not post but a foreign alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign character.

clue.text: Unacceptable ruling about backing up

indicators.note: about means going round, so the ruling word wraps the reversed piece

parts.note: regnant means reigning, ruling

indicators.note: backing tells us the word up is turned to run the other way

explanation.surface: A judgement or ruling that cannot be accepted when it comes to supporting something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses 'up', and 'about' has the word for ruling (reigning, as a monarch) go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repugnant is so distasteful or offensive that it cannot be accepted.

clue.text: Later consequences of getting me that far drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters of me that far are jumbled

explanation.surface: Hangover regret after drinking so heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges METHATFAR; 'of getting' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the period of effects following an event.

clue.text: Backward-looking group of reporters with a bygone style

indicators.note: looking backward means the letters are read in reverse order
a group of letters is taken from inside the word reporters

explanation.surface: A nostalgic gang of journalists dressed in an old-fashioned manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward-looking' seems to be the definition, but it reverses ORTER, the letters taken by 'group of' from inside 'reporters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes things deliberately imitating fashions of an earlier era.

clue.text: Show soldiers meat from farm animal

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
veal is meat from a calf

explanation.surface: Showing soldiers the meat from a farm beast.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or display, so to show.

clue.text: Miserable person, head down to go to be sick

indicators.note: the head, the opening letter, is to go, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a wretch is an unhappy or pitiable person

explanation.surface: A sorry figure, head lowered, heads off to throw up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head down to go' removes the first letter W from WRETCH; 'to' joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave as if vomiting, so it means being sick.

clue.text: Part of ship finished in stoppage

parts.note: the hold is a cargo space in a ship
time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: A section of a ship ended up in a blockage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is a delay that stops progress.

clue.text: I'm nervous about being infested

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of I'm nervous are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about catching an infestation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges IMNERVOUS; 'being' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Verminous means overrun with vermin such as lice or rats, i.e. infested.

clue.text: Short paragraph's given backing for criminal charge

parts.note: par is a short form of paragraph; the 's is just 'is'. That the letters also sit inside the word paragraph is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A brief bit of text supporting a charge in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given backing' turns PAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap' or a rap sheet.

clue.text: Piper, perhaps noble, keeping time

indicators.note: keeping means holding in, so the word for noble surrounds the time letter

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A noble piper keeping the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piper, perhaps' points to the tongue-twister Peter Piper, who picked a peck of pickled peppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Piper of the nursery rhyme is one example of someone with this first name.

clue.text: Practical program deliberately gave wrong answer

parts.note: an app is a computer program
to give a false answer on purpose is to lie, past tense lied

explanation.surface: Software that knowingly answered incorrectly in a practical test.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied science or maths is put to practical use, as opposed to pure theory.

clue.text: A little pasty? One must get stuck into exercises

indicators.note: getting stuck into something means going inside it

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A slightly pale person told they must throw themselves into workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like pale, but is the pastry; the question mark flags a pie as a sort of pasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasty is a pastry-wrapped filling, close kin to a small pie.

clue.text: Not appropriate to sleep inside it

indicators.note: inside places the word for sleep within the word it

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Saying it is unsuitable to sleep in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or ill-fitting for the circumstances.

clue.text: Girl with nipper is a mean individual

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name
something that nips is a pincher

explanation.surface: A girl with a small child turns out to be stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' looks like a child but here means something that pinches.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny-pincher is a miser, someone mean with money.
